narrative: Demand for PL1__ME4BA165 is near-continuous (98.9% non-zero working days) with moderate variability (CV=0.357) and a left-skewed distribution, indicating consistently high throughput with occasional dips. Lead times are unstable (CV=0.362), exhibiting a bimodal pattern around 2 and 4 days that contributes 74.87% of total demand-during-lead-time variance. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy with EOQ-optimised order quantity of 4,652 units and statistically-derived safety stock of 782 units is recommended to achieve the 95% service level while reducing total annual inventory costs by 68.8%.
warnings: Lead time CV=0.362 classified as unstable; bimodal distribution suggests two distinct supplier delivery modes — investigate with supplier
Safety stock raised significantly from SAP baseline 79 to recommended 782 to reflect true demand-during-lead-time uncertainty
Storage utilisation at 96.59% post-replenishment (5,434/5,626 units); monitor capacity headroom closely
SAP safety lead time of 4.0 days should be reduced to ~2.0 days once statistical safety stock is implemented

research_insights.selection_rationale: Near-continuous demand (98.9% non-zero days) with moderate CV justifies a continuous-review reorder-point policy. EOQ minimises the sum of annual ordering and holding costs given ~97,857 units annual demand, unit cost of $3.77, holding rate 12%, and ordering cost $50.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage utilisation reaches 96.59% immediately after replenishment, leaving only ~192 units of headroom. Any demand surge or early delivery could transiently exceed capacity. Recommend reviewing max_storage_units with the warehouse team and considering a small reduction in order_quantity if capacity is operationally binding.
